head: claude/prop-fills-gap-20260901
title: prop: place a fill by every instant it carries, not one mutable field (prop_fills_stale false positive)
body:
## What this is

The `prop_fills_stale` banner on `breakout_1` — latched at severity `alert` since 2026-08-30T19:33:29Z — is a **false positive**. The prop journal is **not** missing the trade. This PR fixes the detector defect that manufactured it, and files the finding.

**Draft on purpose. Do not merge on my say-so — the manager owns the merge.**

## The defect

`prop_fills_staleness.assess_balance_move` filtered fills on `reported_at`. `prop_journal.insert_fill` is idempotent, and its UPDATE branch **overwrites `reported_at` with `now`** on every re-report while preserving `created_at`. So a corrective re-report — routine on a manual bridge — can push an already-reported close **out of the window it explains**.

The live instance, `prop_fills` id 41 (SOLUSDT long 49 @ 105.04 → 105.76, `pnl` 35.28, `closed`), against window `(2026-08-30T13:37:39.446290Z, 2026-08-30T19:33:29.584285Z]`:

| field | value | vs. window end |
|---|---|---|
| `created_at` | `2026-08-30T19:33:17.466421Z` | **12.1 s inside** |
| `reported_at` | `2026-08-30T19:39:00.972519Z` | 5 m 31 s outside |

The row's own `reason` carries an explicit `CORRECTION:`. Latch state read live: `{"balance:18->19": {… "fills_in_window": 0}}`.

## Why this is worth a backlog row and not a quiet fix

`BL-20260825-PROP-FILLS-RECORD-WHEN-THEY-WERE-REPORTED-NOT-WHEN-THEY-TRADED` explicitly checked this module and concluded: *"NOT A DETECTOR REGRESSION, checked rather than assumed. `prop_fills_staleness` is unaffected: its B arm asks were any fills REPORTED between these two balance snapshots, for which `reported_at` is the correct field."*

That check was right about **which question** the field answers and missed that the field is **mutable**. `reported_at` records *when this was last reported*, not *whether it was reported by then* — and a membership test over a closed historical window cannot rest on a field later writes can move.

This is the **third** prop consumer to key an event-time question on a report-time field (`BL-20260828`, `prop_reconcile.snapshot_plus_fills`, rendered a false static-DD floor breach of −19.29; `BL-20260825`, the measurement gap). It is also the desensitized-alarm P1 arriving *inside* the detector built to avoid it — and the design makes it **unclearable by the operator**, since a `balance_moved_unreported` latch is pruned only when a newer snapshot supersedes the pair.

## The change

Membership is now `any` of `fill_evidence_times(fill)`:

- **`created_at`** — immutable first report (set only on INSERT); fixes the mutability defect.
- **`reported_at`** — kept, back-compat: a fill first reported before the window and re-reported inside it genuinely was reported inside it.
- **`closed_at`** — the venue's own trade time; the only field that can place a *late backfill* in the window it repairs.
- **`opened_at` deliberately EXCLUDED** — an open is not evidence that a *realized* move was reported, so counting it would let an opening report explain a close nobody reported.

Plus `fills_in_window_bases`, naming which instant placed each counted fill — `None` before counting, `{}` after, so *we did not count* stays distinct from *we counted and nothing matched*.

## Measured, stating the population

All 19 live `prop_account_status` rows for `breakout_1` = **18 consecutive pairs**, re-graded through the patched pure function at threshold $25.00:

- **Exactly one verdict changes**: `18->19`, `unreported` → `explained`, `fills_in_window_bases {"created_at": 1}`.
- **Control holds**: the genuine 2026-08-20 → 08-23 −$111.86 gap (`10->11`) still grades `unreported`. The basis was widened without blunting the detector.

## Is anything actually missing? No.

- Whole-history ledger (snapshot 1 → 19): balance move **−$427.93** vs **−$366.87** of reported closed-fill `pnl`; residual **−$61.06** over 14 round trips ≈ all-in commissions, several of which the rows' own `reason` says are excluded from `pnl`.
- Every non-skipped prop position has a closed fill. Detector A latched nothing.
- **The report-back path is not broken again** — fill id 41 was ingested *and* corrected on 2026-08-30. This is not a recurrence of the 404-ing screenshot reader from `BL-20260823`; what did not hold is the detector built in response to it.
- **No operator ask, and none should be made.** No screenshot is needed. **No fill was written and the prop journal is untouched.**

## Deliberately unchanged — the design forbids each

- No coupling to `list_tickets` / `find_unacted_tickets` / `prop_reconcile`. The existing no-import test is untouched and still passes.
- Fills are still **not** required to reconcile with the delta. The question stays *was anything reported*.
- `balance_moved_unreported` latches are still pruned **silently**, never with an `[OK]`.

## Residual this does not fix

`closed_at` is populated on **4 of 41** live fills (4 of the 18 `closed` rows), so a backfill usually still cannot be dated into the window it repairs. Measured: the original `BL-20260823` −$111.86 gap **was** repaired — fill id 33, a 2026-08-22 round trip at −111.77 — and still grades `unreported`, because that row carries its close time only in prose. Already filed as `BL-20260825` (an ingest gap; both columns exist). ⚠️ Do not read a persistent `unreported` as proof of a missing trade without first checking for a backfill that cannot be dated.

## Verification, and what was NOT run

⚠️ **pytest and lint-imports are absent from this sandbox.** 39 pure tests were exercised under a stdlib harness — all pre-existing pure tests plus **12 new** — 0 failures. **11 fixture-based (`monkeypatch`) tests in this file were NOT run** and must go green in CI. Every `BL-`/`MB-` id cited in the module was checked to resolve against a real backlog row.

## After merge

No state-file surgery is needed **or permitted**. On the next cadence window (`PROP_FILLS_STALENESS_CHECK_SECONDS`, default 3600 s) after the trader restarts on the merged sha, pair `18->19` re-grades `explained`, `findings` goes empty, and `stale_fill_accounts()` drops the account — the banner clears itself. **If it does not clear, the deploy did not take, and that is the finding.**
